summary: Target-level plan of the explicit side of P.3: the coordinate 22-term relation, generic vector configurations and the weight-three Bigrassmannian complex, the three configuration maps r₄=−3·Alt₄, r₅ and r₆=−(1/5)·Alt₆ of the triple ratio, which are 18 times Goncharov's f₀, f₁ and M₃, the geometric presentation and its comparison with B₃, duality, the comparison from the homology of GL and from rank-filtered rational K-theory, the transfer on H³, the descent of L₃, the Borel class and the every-family determinant for ζ_F(3). 27 nodes, 73 API items, 37 unit tests and 15 named theorems, all with signatures in the suggested file, which elaborates at the pinned Mathlib. Six mathematical gaps and five supplier requests are recorded; P.3 is planned, not closed, and nothing is claimed formalised.

nodes.title: Coordinate 22-term relation
nodes.statement: In Q[F], write [z] for the basis vector. Set A=ca−a+1 and B=bc−c+1. Define R(a,b,c)=Cyc₃([A]+[A/(ca)]+[c]+[B/(Ab)]−[A/c]+[−Ba/A]−[B/(Abc)]−[1])+[−abc], with Cyc₃ over (a,b,c),(c,a,b),(b,c,a). Its admissible locus requires a,b,c and all three cyclic A,B to be nonzero. The [1] terms are retained; values 1 or −1 are allowed. This construction is a formal relation, not a second definition of B₃. The admissible locus is larger than the locus of the seven-point configurations of the source's geometric relation (1.10): with x₁,x₂,x₃ the coordinate vertices, z=(1,1,1) and side points (1,a,0), (0,1,b), (c,0,1), the value a=1 (or b=1, c=1) puts z on a line through a vertex and a side point, and abc=−1 makes the three side points collinear. For those parameters the relation is the source's specialisation of the generic one, and its vanishing in B₃ is a statement to prove, not part of the generic generator set.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; all coefficient modules are rational unless specified otherwise.
proofSteps: Use Finsupp.single for symbols and finite sums for the cyclic operator.
Expand (1.16), correcting the omitted minus sign inside the sixth argument: −a(bc−c+1)/(ca−a+1). The geometric relation (1.10) and the c=1 specialization fix this sign.

Relate its image to the parent quotient relation submodule: for generic parameters R(a,b,c) is the parent's generator in coordinates; for a, b or c equal to 1, or abc=−1, use the source's specialisation (its (1.17) is shown on p. 209 to be a sum of three generic relations) and state the result rationally.
acceptance: After δ₃ and then δ₂⊗1, the image of R(a,b,c) in Λ²U⊗U is zero in every prime-valuation coordinate at (2,2,2), (1,2,3), (−1,2,5), (3,1/2,5/7) and (1,1/2,4/3).
The same computation with the positive sixth argument printed in the source is nonzero at (2,2,2) and at (1,2,3); this is the test that fixes the sign of the sixth argument without any analysis.

nodes.statement: For every admissible R(a,b,c), δ₃(eval R)=0 in B₂(F)⊗U_F, where U_F=F×⊗Q and δ₃[z]₃=[z]₂⊗u(z), with u(1)=0. This proves that the explicit coordinate relation is killed, rather than replacing explicit B₃ by the conjecturally larger inductive B₃.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; all coefficient modules are rational unless specified otherwise.
proofSteps: Use GR Lemma 5.1 to replace each mixed symbol {x,y}₂,₁ by its six ordinary B₃ symbols, including −{1}₃.

In Proposition 5.4 collect the determinant-unit coefficients; each remaining coefficient is two five-term relations or the displayed sum of three five-term relations.
Apply the supplier’s rational B₂ inversion and five-term identities; specialize only along the admissible locus.

nodes.title: Generic vector configurations
nodes.statement: A generic m-tuple in F^q has every subfamily of size at most q linearly independent. Let C_m(q) be Q[generic m-tuples] modulo the span of [g·l]−[l] for g∈GL_q(F). This is the free Q-module on GL-orbits. Individual vector rescalings are not quotiented out. Deletion removes a vector; projection removes l_i and projects the others to F^q/F l_i, whose identification with F^(q−1) is immaterial in the orbit quotient.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; all coefficient modules are rational unless specified otherwise.
proofSteps: Define the generic subtype using native LinearIndependent on injectively indexed subfamilies.

Use native Representation.Coinvariants of the rational permutation representation on the generic subtype. Its kernel is the span of [g·l]−[l], so the source presentation agrees with that existing quotient.
Use a linear equivalence from the one-dimensional quotient complement to define each projection face; different choices differ by GL.
acceptance: Over an infinite field the complex of generic tuples with the deletion differential is acyclic in positive degrees (G95 Lemma 2.11), so C_•(q) receives the group homology of GL_q(F); the definition must make this statement provable.
The classes of (1,2) and (1,3) in C₂(1) over Q are different, and the class of a tuple is unchanged by a simultaneous change of basis but not by rescaling one vector.
A tuple of fewer than q vectors is generic exactly when it is linearly independent; a tuple of at least q vectors is generic exactly when every q of them form a basis.

nodes.title: Weight-three Bigrassmannian complex
nodes.statement: BC_m^(3)=⊕_{3≤q<m} C_m(q), in homological degree m, starting at degree 4. Set ∂=Σ_i(−1)^i deletion_i and p=Σ_i(−1)^i projection_i, with zero-based indices. Each lowers tuple size by one; projection also lowers q. With these face signs ∂p+p∂=0, so D=∂+p. Components leaving 3≤q<m are zero; this is the quotient by the lower rows, not a subcomplex obtained by simply dropping outgoing maps.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; all coefficient modules are rational unless specified otherwise.
proofSteps: Prove the two same-kind face identities and the mixed identity before taking signed sums.
Use the native finite direct sum of the orbit modules and assemble the two differential components.
Check D²=0, including the q=3 boundary and the m=q+1 corner.
acceptance: On C₇(4) the component of D² in C₅(3) is ∂p+p∂, which is zero for the zero-based face signs; with the opposite relative sign it is 2∂p≠0.
Degree 4 is C₄(3) alone and degree 3 is zero, so the complex starts where the source's weight-three complex starts.

nodes.title: Configuration chain comparison
nodes.statement: With the common normalization above, d₂r₅=r₄∂ on C₅(3), δ₃r₆=r₅∂ on C₆(3), and r₄p=r₅p=r₆p=0 on C₅(4), C₆(4), C₇(4) respectively. Together with the seven-term relation these components give a degree-reversed chain map BC_•^(3)→Γ(F,3), supported in degrees 6,5,4.

nodes.statement: The parent single-valued function L₃(z)=Re(Li₃(z)−log|z|Li₂(z)+(1/3)log²|z|Li₁(z)), continuously extended at 0 and 1, induces a Q-linear L₃:B₃(C)→R. Conjugate embeddings have equal coordinates.

nodes.title: Conditional transfer on the complex
nodes.statement: Assume the weight-four homotopy/residue resolution of Gon95 Conjecture 1.39: Γ(F(t),4)/Γ(F,4)→⊕_P Γ(F[t]/P,3)[−1] is a quasi-isomorphism, for monic irreducible P, with all maps interpreted in the derived category. For E=F[t]/P, insert its summand, invert this quasi-isomorphism and take minus the residue at infinity. After cancelling the shift this constructs a derived transfer Γ(E,3)→Γ(F,3). Its H³ map must agree with the previously constructed Milnor transfer. No unconditional B₃ or termwise transfer is inferred.

nodes.title: Geometric trilogarithm presentation
nodes.statement: Let G₃(F) be the rational module on PGL₃-orbits of arbitrary ordered six-tuples of native points of P²(F). Impose: a tuple is zero if two points coincide or four are collinear; the alternating seven-term deletion relation; and the intersection relation R3 of GR (148). For triangle vertices a₁,a₂,a₃ and b_i on a_i a_{i+1}, write T(z) for its tuple with invariant z=r′(b₁|a₂,a₃,b₂,b₃), where r′(u,v,w,x)=(u−w)(v−x)/((u−x)(v−w)). Put T₁(z)=−T(z)−2T(1−z)+T(1). For a type-B tuple y=(x₁,x₂,m,x₃,x₄,x₅) with m=x₁x₂∩x₃x₄, impose 3[y]=Σ_{i=1}⁵(−1)^(i−1) T₁(r′(y₆|y₁,…,ŷ_i,…,y₅)), wherever these projected configurations are defined. This auxiliary geometric group is compared with the parent B₃; it is not substituted for its definition. These are the conventions of GR §7.3, and they are mutually consistent: the seven-term relation applied to T(z) together with a generic point, and R3, give the class whose image is [z]₃. Goncharov's 1995 Definition 1.5 uses the inverse cross-ratio (1.6), for which the bracket −[x]−2[1−x]+[1] changes sign (his (8.1)); with his relation as printed the triangle in the order (a₁,a₂,a₃,b₁,b₂,b₃) has image −[z]₃, and it is the order of his Fig. 1.12 that has image +[z]₃ (E-P3-08).
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; coefficient groups are rational.
proofSteps: Use native Projectivization F (F³) for points and the native Finsupp module for ordered tuples.
Generate a rational relation submodule from simultaneous projective GL changes and the three displayed families; take the native quotient.
Degenerate T(1) is retained via the triangle specialization of the source; do not exclude it by requiring every six-tuple to be generic.
Derive permutation antisymmetry from the seven-term relation with a repeated point (Gon95 Lemma 1.7).
Use triangle representatives e₁,e₂,e₃,(1,1,0),(0,1,1),(−z,0,1), whose projected invariant is z; this also gives a concrete nonzero representative at z=1.

The type-B locus is injective, its third point lies in both spans of the first/second and fourth/fifth points, and projection from its sixth point has pairwise nonzero minors. The intersection generator is explicitly 3[y] minus the alternating sum of T₁ of these projected ratios.
acceptance: Evaluating L₃∘M₃ from the seven-term relation and R3 alone, on T(z) together with a generic seventh point, gives L₃(z) for z=0.37+0.52i, −1.3+0.2i and 2.5−1.1i.

The type-B and type-C values so obtained change sign under each transposition of points on a common line or of generic points, and the seven-term relation holds for seven points of which four are collinear.
A tuple with two equal points, or with four collinear points, represents zero; T(1), with collinear side points, does not.

nodes.title: Geometric–symbol trilogarithm comparison
nodes.statement: There is a canonical rational isomorphism M₃:G₃(F)≃B₃(F). It sends T(z) to [z]₃. On type-B configurations use one third of the alternating five-term sum of T₁-values from (148), evaluated by T₁(z)=−[z]₃−2[1−z]₃+[1]₃. On generic six-tuples choose the intersection m of the first two and next two point lines, and use the seven-term relation to reduce to types B and C. The result is independent of the auxiliary intersection choice. On generic six-tuples M₃=−(1/90)·Alt₆[T_raw]₃, with T_raw the determinant triple ratio of the triple-ratio node and Alt₆ the unnormalised alternation; equivalently Alt₆M₃=720·M₃=−8·Alt₆[T_raw]₃ and r₆=18·M₃. The source's Proposition 7.2 prints the constant 3/2 in place of −8 (E-P3-06). Integrally Gon95 states the comparison only modulo 6-torsion; rationalization removes that qualification.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; coefficient groups are rational.
proofSteps: Use the triangle specialization to define the symbol-to-geometric map.
The corrected coordinate relation gives the relations among triangle classes; the geometric R3 gives the reverse evaluation.
Apply the seven-term reduction to the generic case and the projected five-point reduction to type C.
GR Lemmas 7.3–7.4 cancel the type-B alternating terms and identify the remaining type-C contribution with the triple ratio.

Fix the constant: by the seven-term relation each generic M₃ is an alternating sum of two type-B and four type-C values, each one third of a sum of T′-brackets. After skew-symmetrisation the type-B values vanish (GR Lemma 7.3) and the surviving type-C terms are of the kind treated in GR Lemma 7.4, each a multiple of (3/2)·Alt₆[T]₃. Their total is −8·Alt₆[T]₃, that is a total coefficient −16/3 on the expression of Lemma 7.4; the count of the surviving terms with their signs is the bookkeeping the source omits, and it is the content of the first gap. Establish Alt₆[T]₃=−90·M₃ in explicit B₃ before transferring seven-term and duality identities.
acceptance: For generic six-tuples of C³, the L₃-value of M₃ computed from the seven-term relation and R3 does not depend on which of three auxiliary intersection points is used, and equals −1/90 of the L₃-value of Alt₆[T_raw]₃ to ten digits.
The same value tends to L₃(z) along generic tuples tending to T(z).
The constant 3/2 would give 1/480 in place of −1/90 and is excluded by both checks.

nodes.title: Configuration duality
nodes.statement: For 0<q<m, the kernel of the surjective column map F^m→F^q associated to a generic m-tuple has dimension m−q. Choosing a basis of that kernel and taking its coordinate columns gives a generic m-tuple in F^(m−q); another basis changes it by GL. This defines a linear equivalence *:C_m(q)≃C_m(m−q). Equivalently, annihilator duality on the generic Grassmannian gives the same map. Under the natural dimension identifications it is involutive. It exchanges deletion with projection and descends further through independent vector scaling to the projective configuration duality.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; coefficient groups are rational.
proofSteps: Identify the tuple with the row subspace of its full-rank q×m matrix; the dual row subspace is its annihilator.
Nonzero complementary minors show the dual tuple is generic.
For a matrix (I_q,B), the dual is (−Bᵀ,I_{m−q}); in the square case, normalize the first block to get −(B⁻¹)ᵀ.
Double annihilation proves involutivity, and taking a coordinate hyperplane exchanges deletion with quotient projection.
Use Gon95 Proposition 7.1 and Lemmas 7.2–7.5 for the geometric intersection description and Corollary 7.6 for the face identity.
acceptance: For q=2, m=4 and the vectors (1,0),(0,1),(1,2),(1,3) the dual class is that of (−1,−1),(−2,−3),(1,0),(0,1), computed from a basis of the kernel; it is not the class of (1,0),(0,1),(3,−2),(−1,1).
Prototype general q,m duality, not only the square case: use explicit Fin dimension transports for double duality and the deletion/projection identity.

nodes.title: Trilogarithm antisymmetry under duality
nodes.statement: For a projective six-tuple with no four collinear points, its dual represents the negative of its class in G₃(F). Consequently M₃(*x)=−M₃(x), and the alternating triple-ratio map satisfies r₆ p=0 on C₇(4). This is an equality in the geometric quotient and then in the parent explicit B₃, not merely a functional identity of real regulators.
hypotheses: F is an infinite field; coefficient groups are rational.

Describe the dual as the six hyperplanes attached to the two triangles by Corollary 7.6.
Pair the 46 original terms with the dual terms; identical projected configurations have opposite signs.
For the remaining pairs use L′₃(x)=−[x]₃−2[1−x]₃+[1]₃ and the identities in (8.1); Lemma 8.2 supplies the three exceptional projection comparisons.
Use deletion/projection duality and the seven-term relation in the dual C₇(3) configuration to obtain top projection vanishing.

The hypothesis is that no four points are collinear, as in the source; it is weaker than genericity.
